sourceInformation.genre: Arcade vehicular arena shooter; ricochet duels and dogfighting
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), native node materials and WebGPURenderer (WebGPU primary, WebGL 2 fallback); Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; WebRTC; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0; esbuild 0.25.11
sourceInformation.artDirection: Stylized cel-shaded paper-and-ink tabletop diorama; procedural low-poly tanks and biplanes, warm sand, teal shadows, ink outlines
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframe tracks for tank rumble, cannon recoil, propellers, and barrel rolls; procedural movement and particles
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated Web Audio chiptune march, synthesized sound effects and Animalese-style gibberish; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: Host-authoritative AI Hub shared-world sessions for 1–4 players; standalone two-player WebRTC direct-link duel with manual invitation/reply; two-player couch versus
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153 with software WebGPU and WebGL 2; 68 automated checks covering a four-heat playthrough, swept collisions, ricochets, pickups, respawn, ghost tanks, aircraft wrapping, menus, live tuning, standard-mapped controller emulation, 390 x 844 multitouch, Web Audio signal analysis, two-page WebRTC, and AI Hub conformance. Hub scenarios include 2 and 4 players, 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter, 5% packet loss, host departure and a playerless server; normal rendered sessions and graphics-free protocol stress tests. Screenshots used only for visual review. Physical controller, physical touch device and real-world cross-network connectivity: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: none; native model knowledge only. Supplied AI Hub integration files fetched as implementation requirements; no internet searches.

testingFeedback: Four implementation defects were caught and fixed during verification: duplicate Enter activation, an invalid texture binding after repeated arena transitions, delayed Hub readiness during shader warm-up, and slow standalone peer-departure detection. Two test-fixture mistakes were also corrected; those were not game defects.
Two were game breaking: the texture binding could stop rendering, and delayed readiness could prevent a Hub round from starting.
The complete four-heat browser playthrough combined with the supplied Hub conformance harness. The final suite passed 68 of 68 checks, including normal rendered two- and four-player sessions.
Initial software-WebGPU screenshots: the canvas could be blank or lose the device during capture. State checks verified WebGPU; WebGL fallback captures were more useful for visual review.
engineFeedback: Three.js native AnimationMixer clips and node-based cel materials fit the toy-diorama style well, and WebGPURenderer shares scene code across WebGPU and its WebGL fallback.

Yes. Legacy material translation produced a missing texture binding after repeated transitions. Native node materials and explicit texture nodes resolved it. Shader warm-up also had to be separated from Hub readiness.
The complete combat simulation and host-authoritative multiplayer layer, including swept Rapier queries for ricochets, scoring, respawns, snapshots, input transport and round lifecycle.
Managing texture and scene lifetimes across tank, ghost and air rounds, and testing multiple software-rendered browser copies without confusing graphics stalls with protocol failures.
none; the engine packages were not modified. All adaptations are in application code.
Provide texture-binding errors that identify the material, object and missing property, with a clearer asynchronous readiness path for embedded multiplayer games.
promptFeedback: The precise controller-first requirements, attract mode, reproducible environment details and supplied multiplayer contract made the intended finished experience clear.

The ban on internet research sits alongside a required online integration repository. I treated the supplied integration files and pinned dependency downloads as implementation requirements, and performed no internet searches.
Making keyboard, mouse, controller and assisted multitouch behave consistently across solo, couch, direct-link and Hub play, then exercising those paths without physical devices.
Clarify the expected standalone connection method and whether a TURN relay should be supplied. Explicitly distinguish required integration-document retrieval from internet research.

aiHub.name: Combrisk
aiHub.description: A pocket-sized ricochet rivalry inspired by Combat (1977). Battle through four arcade heats with bank-shot scoring, ghost tanks and biplanes, or settle a score in couch and online duels.
aiHub.controls: Left stick move, right stick aim, R2/RT fire, L1/LB or Cross/A boost; WASD + mouse, click/Space fire, Shift boost; touch: invisible dual sticks with assisted aim and fire.
